s: Hello and welcome to Word Kitchen!
Today we talk about travel and transport.
A car is a small road vehicle with four wheels.
A car takes you from home to work, or to the shops.
I drive my car to work every day.
A bus is a big vehicle.
Many people ride in a bus.
A bus is bigger than a car.
I take the bus to the city.
I read a book on the bus.
A bus stop is near my house.
Last week I took the train to my mother's house.
The train was clean and quiet.
Trains are great for long trips.
A train can be faster than a car.
A taxi is a car you pay to take you somewhere.
When I am late, I take a taxi.
A taxi is fast, but a taxi is not cheap.
The taxi driver was very kind.
A plane flies in the sky.
A plane is the fastest way to travel.
My first plane trip was to London.
I like to sit by the window in a plane.
You ride a bike with your legs.
A bike is good for short trips.
My son has a new bike.
On Sundays we ride our bikes in the park.
A ticket is a small paper.
You need a ticket for the train.
You need a ticket for the plane.
A ticket can be cheap or dear.
A road is a long hard path.
Cars and buses use the road.
The road to the airport is long.
A wide road is good for a bike.
A station is the place where trains and buses stop.
I waited at the station for my friend.
A station has many people in the morning.
An airport is the big place where planes take off and land.
I was at the airport at six in the morning.
My plane left the airport at eight.
I say a word, and you think of the meaning.
A small vehicle with four wheels.
A big vehicle for many people.
The place for trains and buses.
Let's say them one last time: car, bus, train, taxi, plane, bike, ticket, road, station, airport.
Thank you for listening to Word Kitchen!
Practice these words, and see you tomorrow!
